video_goal: Demonstrate how to assemble and secure white plastic hangers into a large snowflake for winter decoration.
required_subjects_and_props: 16 white plastic tubular hangers, clear zip ties, wire cutters, red winter ribbon, flat work surface, door wreath hook.

outline_steps.visual_action: Hands place a stack of 16 white plastic tubular hangers and a bag of clear zip ties onto a flat wooden table.
Hands take two white plastic hangers and align their long bottom straight edges together, positioning the hooks to face outward in opposite directions.
Fingers thread a clear zip tie around the aligned bottom edges of the two hangers, pulling the tail through the head until it clicks tightly.
Hands arrange four pairs of the zip-tied hangers into a plus-sign shape on the table, with all plastic hooks pointing outward.
Hands thread a clear zip tie through the center intersection where the four hanger pairs meet, pulling it tight to secure the core of the snowflake.
Hands place four additional pairs of hangers diagonally between the first four pairs, forming an 8-point symmetrical snowflake pattern.
Fingers wrap and tighten zip ties around the overlapping plastic hooks and straight edges where the diagonal hangers intersect the base cross.
Hands move systematically around the outer perimeter of the snowflake, securing all remaining loose connection points with clear zip ties.
A pair of metal wire cutters snips off the long, protruding tails of the clear zip ties flush with their locking heads.
Hands wrap and tie a thick, red winter-themed ribbon into a decorative bow around the top-most plastic hanger hook.
Hands lift the completed, large white plastic hanger snowflake and place its top hook onto a metal wreath hanger on a front door.
